summary: Partition 1 (Zustand studio store, route utils, dev-server /ontology routing, package deps) introduces no CRITICAL or MAJOR defects. Core invariants hold: no Graph A / CanonicalBusinessConcept model changes (SHA-256 stability unaffected); ONT-EVO-001 is enforced client-side by blocking all destructive/unexpressible mutations and emitting only additive OntologyDelta ops; ONT-EVO-002 is gated pre-commit using an authoritatively recomputed scorecard with per-URI waiver coverage; ONT-EVO-003 OCC is honored via If-Match on head_sha256 for delta commit and dual If-Match on promotion. Session isolation and stale-response guards are consistently applied across async actions. No production mocks, no hardcoded URLs (API base is injectable/env-driven), and the dev-server catch-all only serves index.html, so it introduces no traversal surface. Remaining findings are minor robustness items: the post-commit baseline relies on client snapshots with silent fallback to stale head SHA/version, the client grounding derivation treats unscored mappings as GROUNDED (0.85 default), waivers are not re-scoped to the head SHA they were issued against, the promotion SHA-missing check is dead code, there are a few normalization inconsistencies in delta generation and diff, and edits are not locked during an in-flight commit. Server-side enforcement must remain authoritative for ONT-EVO-002/003.

findings.title: Post-commit head SHA/version silently fall back to stale values; baseline not reconciled with server
findings.description: On commit success, head_sha256 is set to `data.target_sha256 || data.head_sha256 || state.activeSession.head_sha256` and active_version falls back to the old version. If the server response omits these, the store keeps the pre-commit head. The next commit then sends a stale If-Match (guaranteed 412) and recomputes the same target_version. In addition, committedNodes/committedEdges are set to the client-sent snapshot rather than the server's canonical result, so any server-side normalization (derived grounding, trimmed definitions) makes later deltas diverge from server truth. promoteWorkspace treats a missing SHA as an error, so the two paths are inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Require target_sha256 in the commit response (emit a PROMOTION_SHA_MISSING-style error toast if absent), use the computed targetVersion as the fallback instead of the old version, and reload the head graph from the server after a successful commit (when there are no further edits) to re-baseline committedNodes/Edges.

findings.title: deriveGroundingStatus grounds any concept that has an unscored mapping
findings.description: When mappings exist but none carry a numeric confidence, avgConf defaults to `explicitConfidence ?? 0.85`, which yields GROUNDED. addConcept/updateConcept do not validate mapping target_uri or scheme. A user can therefore add an arbitrary or empty-URI mapping, or pass confidence 1.0, to make a concept GROUNDED and get through the client-side ONT-EVO-002 commit gate. The server must stay authoritative, but the client gate is weaker than the invariant states.
findings.recommendation: Treat mappings without confidence as LOW_CONFIDENCE (or require confidence), reject mappings with an empty or invalid target_uri, and do not let a caller-supplied node confidence override mapping-derived confidence. Document that server-side ONT-EVO-002 validation is the enforcement point.

findings.title: Waiver validity is not checked against waived_base_sha256
findings.description: recomputeScorecard accepts any sessionWaivers entry with waiver_applied=true, whatever its waived_base_sha256. Waivers therefore keep applying after later commits and promotions move the head. Coverage is per-URI, so new ungrounded concepts still FAIL, which limits the impact. Still, a waiver issued against base SHA X keeps passing the gate at head Y with no re-authorization.
findings.recommendation: Either scope waiver validity to the head lineage (e.g. invalidate or flag when waived_base_sha256 is not an ancestor or equal of the current head), or explicitly document that waivers persist per-URI across versions and that the server re-validates on delta/promote.

findings.title: promoteWorkspace SHA-missing guard is unreachable; local commit record is fabricated
findings.description: `newSha = promoData.head_sha256 || currentSession.head_sha256`, and currentSession.head_sha256 was already required to equal req.head_sha256 (non-empty). The PROMOTION_SHA_MISSING branch can never fire, so a promotion response without a SHA is accepted silently. The appended SessionCommit uses a client-generated `commit-${Date.now()}` id and a client timestamp rather than server-provided data. promoteWorkspace also does not block while isHistoricalView is true.
findings.recommendation: Check `promoData.head_sha256` directly. Prefer server-returned commit metadata, or reload the session after promotion. Add an isHistoricalView guard for consistency with commitChanges.

findings.title: refine_definition compares definitions without undefined/empty normalization
findings.description: commitChanges emits refine_definition when `node.definition !== committed.definition`, while updateConcept and computeDiff normalize with `(x || "")`. A definition that goes from undefined to "" (e.g. after an editor round-trip) emits a spurious refine_definition op and a PATCH bump with no semantic change.
findings.recommendation: Compare `(node.definition || "") !== (committed.definition || "")` to match the other comparison sites.

findings.title: addRelationship accepts node.id endpoints but commit emits them as concept URIs
findings.description: Endpoint validation matches either `n.concept_uri` or `n.id`, but the edge is stored unchanged, and commitChanges emits `endpoints: [edge.source_concept_uri, edge.target_concept_uri]`. If a canvas caller passes a node id that differs from its concept_uri (possible for addConcept nodes whose id was not set to the URI), the delta carries dangling endpoints that the server will reject or persist incorrectly. The ONT-DAG check also keys adjacency by concept_uri and would miss these edges.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the matched node and rewrite source/target to the canonical concept_uri before storing the edge, or validate against concept_uri only.

findings.title: computeDiff returns an empty diff when base === target even if the working draft has edits
findings.description: Without a baseGraph, computeDiff short-circuits to zero records when baseVersion === targetVersion. Comparing the uncommitted working draft against committed head, where both are labelled with the head version, is a primary use case, and it returns 'no changes' while hasUnsavedChanges is true.
findings.recommendation: Drop the short-circuit (the committedNodes vs nodes comparison already handles equality), or only short-circuit when hasUnsavedChanges is false.

findings.title: Graph edits and discardChanges are allowed while a commit is in flight
findings.description: isCommitting only blocks re-entrant commits. If discardChanges runs mid-flight, nodes revert to the pre-commit baseline. After success, committedNodes becomes sentNodes, but nodes stay at the old baseline with hasUnsavedChanges=true. The next commit then sees 'removed concepts' and is blocked by ONT-EVO-001 until the user discards again. Recoverable, but confusing and error-prone.
findings.recommendation: Guard updateConcept/addConcept/addRelationship/discardChanges with an isCommitting check (toast and return), or have the UI disable edit affordances while committing.

findings.title: Confirm the SemVer policy for add_attribute / add_external_mapping
findings.description: Adding attributes to existing concepts yields a PATCH bump. Under standard SemVer, backward-compatible additions are MINOR. If the server's OntologyDelta validator computes or validates target_version differently, commits will be rejected.
findings.recommendation: Align with the server-side version policy (ideally let the server compute target_version, or share the rule via schemas/v1) and add a contract test.

findings.title: useStudioStore is bound to the module singleton
findings.description: createStudioStore(options) supports configurable instances (apiUrl, initialSession), but the hook always reads the global studioStore, so per-instance stores cannot be used by components. Separately, a 409/412 commit failure does not refresh the session head, so the user cannot recover without a manual reload.
findings.recommendation: Expose a React context provider for the store instance, and on 409/412 from /delta re-fetch session metadata so the user can rebase.

findings.title: Split the monolithic store into slices
findings.description: Export serializers, scorecard computation, delta generation and the diff engine are pure functions embedded in a large store module. Unit tests for this partition's logic live in partition 3.
findings.recommendation: Extract delta generation, the diff engine, scorecard and exporters into separate pure modules with focused unit tests, and compose store slices.

positive_highlights: commitChanges emits only additive OntologyDelta ops and explicitly blocks every non-expressible mutation (deletes, renames, archetype/hub/parent changes, attribute type/description/optionality/example changes, mapping removals and mutations, relationship mutations), which is strong ONT-EVO-001 alignment.
The pre-commit ONT-EVO-002 and ONT-DAG-001 gates use an authoritatively recomputed scorecard, not a cached or caller-mutable one; updateQualityScorecard strips waiver and check fields.
OCC is consistently applied: If-Match head_sha256 on delta commit, dual If-Match on promotion, and If-Match answers_sha256 on clarification answers, with weak-ETag normalization.
Session-isolation guards (captured sid plus request-generation counters) are applied after every await across all async actions, preventing cross-session state corruption.
Export serializers escape IRIs, XML (including invalid XML code points), Turtle and YAML strings, so they avoid injection in the generated artifacts.
No hardcoded hosts: the API base URL is injectable via options or OPENDV_API_URL; fetch is dependency-injected with no production mocks.
The dev-server /ontology catch-all only serves index.html and excludes asset extensions, adding no file-system traversal surface.
